DAY. BIRD’S-EYE exposition, high overhead looking straight down then slightly dutch. ONE DEVICE: the frozen river as a pale hard diagonal across a 2:1 frame. Khitan felt tents as dark stamps on white ice, a thin line of hoof-tracks, one white horse and rider tiny on the far bank. Pale paper-white sky, ice glare, granulated snow-wash, dry-brush ice cracks. No faces. No hanbok. Felt, fur, round tents. High-key day ground. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text. No watermark. PAINTED STILL — no faces and no recognisable person: the only figure is one anonymous dark silhouette, a shadow-shape against the light that belongs to the place; the place or object IS the subject. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
